1.explanation: 'lib/features/ordering/BpmnOrderingProvider.js' is responsible for managing and enforcing the rendering/ordering of BPMN elements. The bug report is about Z-ordering (which element appears on top). This provider decides which elements should render over others, so any fix for always rendering groups on top needs a change here. 'lib/draw/BpmnRenderer.js' is responsible for rendering elements, and changes in drawing order or logic might also touch this file, especially if the rendering process is customized per type of BPMN element. These files are directly involved in rendering and ordering BPMN diagram elements, making them bug related.
1.bug_scenario: The bug is that group elements (rectangles with dashed borders labeled as a group) are not rendered on top of all other elements, so newly created elements (like the visible circle in the screenshot overlapping the border) appear on top of the group border—making the group border get hidden or visually interrupted. The expected behavior is for group elements to always visually appear on top.

2.explanation: Rendering order in diagramming libraries is typically managed by an "ordering" or "z-index" provider, which dictates the sequence in which different elements appear on the canvas. The 'BpmnOrderingProvider.js' file, located in the 'ordering' feature, is the most likely place where element stacking logic is handled. If groups are not rendered on top of all other elements, it is probable that their z-order or rendering order is incorrectly set in this file. The 'ordering/index.js' file is included as it may aggregate or register the provider. These files need to be edited to adjust the rendering order so that group elements appear on top of all other diagram elements.
2.bug_scenario: The bug scenario, as depicted in the image and described in the bug report, shows that when a new element is created near the border of a group, the group's border (the dash-dotted rectangle labeled 'my group') is rendered below the newly created element (a circle). This is incorrect—the group's border should always be rendered above the other elements so that it is clearly visible and not obscured.
